source.text: Ταῦτα εἰπὼν Ἰησοῦς ἐξῆλθεν σὺν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ πέραν τοῦ χειμάρρου τοῦ Κεδρὼν ὅπου ἦν κῆπος, εἰς ὃν εἰσῆλθεν αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: These things having said, Jesus went out with the disciples of him across the winter-stream of the Kidron, where was a garden, into which entered he and the disciples of him.

en.L: Having said these things, Jesus went out with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples across the winter stream of the Kidron, where there was a garden, into which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples entered.
en.B: When Jesus had said these things, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went out with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples and crossed the Kidron Valley. A garden was there, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples went into it.
en.R: When Jesus had finished praying, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left the city with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples and crossed over the Kidron Valley. On the other side there was a garden, and Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples went into it.

es.L: Habiendo dicho estas cosas, Jesús salió con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos al otro lado del torrente Cedrón, donde había un huerto, en el cual entraron {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos.
es.B: Dicho esto, Jesús salió con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos y cruzó el torrente Cedrón. Allí había un huerto, y entró en él con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos.
es.R: Cuando Jesús terminó de orar, salió de la ciudad con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos y cruzó el valle del Cedrón. Al otro lado había un huerto, y Jesús entró allí con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos.

fr.L: Ayant dit ces choses, Jésus sortit avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples au-delà du torrent du Cédron, où il y avait un jardin, dans lequel entrèrent {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples.
fr.B: Quand Jésus eut dit ces choses, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sortit avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples et traversa la vallée du Cédron. Il y avait là un jardin, où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} entra avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples.
fr.R: Quand Jésus a eu fini de prier, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a quitté la ville avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a traversé la vallée du Cédron. De l’autre côté, il y avait un jardin, et Jésus y est entré avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples.

sw.L: Baada ya kusema maneno haya, Yesu alitoka pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kwenda ng'ambo ya kijito cha masika cha Kidroni, palipokuwa na bustani, ambamo {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} waliingia.
sw.B: Baada ya Yesu kusema maneno haya, alitoka na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, akavuka bonde la Kidroni. Hapo palikuwa na bustani, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akaingia humo pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.R: Yesu alipomaliza kuomba, aliondoka mjini pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, akavuka bonde la Kidroni. Ng'ambo ya pili kulikuwa na bustani, na Yesu na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wakaingia humo.

vi.L: Sau khi nói những điều này, Đức Giê-xu đi ra với các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sang bên kia khe suối mùa đông Xết-rôn, nơi có một khu vườn mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cùng các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi vào.
vi.B: Nói xong những điều này, Đức Giê-xu đi ra cùng các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và băng qua thung lũng Xết-rôn. Ở đó có một khu vườn, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cùng các môn đồ vào vườn ấy.
vi.R: Khi Đức Giê-xu cầu nguyện xong, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cùng các môn đồ ra khỏi thành và đi qua thung lũng Xết-rôn. Bên kia thung lũng có một khu vườn, và Đức Giê-xu cùng các môn đồ đi vào đó.

ko.L: 예수께서 이것들을 말씀하시고 나서, 그분의 제자들과 함께 기드론 겨울 시내 건너편으로 나가셨다. 그곳에 동산이 있었는데, 그분과 그분의 제자들이 그 안으로 들어갔다.
ko.B: 예수께서 이 말씀을 하신 뒤에 제자들과 함께 나가서 기드론 골짜기를 건너가셨다. 그곳에 동산이 있었는데, 예수께서 제자들과 함께 그 안으로 들어가셨다.
ko.R: 예수께서 기도를 마치시고 제자들과 함께 성을 나가셨다. 그리고 기드론 골짜기를 건너가셨다. 건너편에 동산이 하나 있었는데, 예수께서 제자들과 함께 그리로 들어가셨다.

pt.L: Tendo dito estas coisas, Jesus saiu com os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos para o outro lado da torrente do Cedrom, onde havia um jardim, no qual {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} e os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos entraram.
pt.B: Depois de dizer essas coisas, Jesus saiu com os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos e atravessou o vale do Cedrom. Ali havia um jardim, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} e os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos entraram nele.
pt.R: Quando Jesus terminou de orar, saiu da cidade com os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos e atravessou o vale do Cedrom. Do outro lado havia um jardim, e Jesus e os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos entraram ali.

am.L: ኢየሱስ ይህን ብሎ ከደቀ መዛሙርቱ ጋር ከቄድሮን የክረምት ወንዝ ማዶ ወጣ፤ በዚያም የአትክልት ስፍራ ነበረ፤ ወደዚያውም እርሱና ደቀ መዛሙርቱ ገቡ።
am.B: ኢየሱስ ይህን ከተናገረ በኋላ ከደቀ መዛሙርቱ ጋር ወጥቶ የቄድሮንን ሸለቆ ተሻገረ። በዚያም የአትክልት ስፍራ ነበረ፤ እርሱና ደቀ መዛሙርቱ ወደዚያ ገቡ።
am.R: ኢየሱስ ጸሎቱን ከጨረሰ በኋላ ከደቀ መዛሙርቱ ጋር ከከተማው ወጥቶ የቄድሮንን ሸለቆ ተሻገረ። በሸለቆው ማዶ የአትክልት ስፍራ ነበረ፤ ኢየሱስና ደቀ መዛሙርቱ ወደዚያ ገቡ።

hi.L: ये बातें कहकर यीशु अपने चेलों के साथ किद्रोन के बरसाती नाले के पार निकले, जहाँ एक बग़ीचा था, जिसमें वे ख़ुद और उनके चेले गए।
hi.B: ये बातें कहने के बाद यीशु अपने चेलों के साथ बाहर निकले और किद्रोन घाटी के पार गए। वहाँ एक बग़ीचा था, और यीशु और उनके चेले उसमें गए।
hi.R: प्रार्थना पूरी करने के बाद यीशु अपने चेलों के साथ शहर से बाहर निकले और किद्रोन घाटी पार की। घाटी के दूसरी ओर एक बग़ीचा था, और यीशु और उनके चेले उसमें गए।

ru.L: Сказав это, Иисус вышел со своими учениками за зимний поток Кедрон, где был сад, в который вошёл {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} и {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} ученики.
ru.B: Сказав это, Иисус вышел вместе с учениками и перешёл через долину Кедрон. Там был сад, и {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} вошёл в него со своими учениками.
ru.R: Когда Иисус закончил молиться, {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} вышел из города вместе с учениками и перешёл через долину Кедрон. На другой стороне был сад, и Иисус с учениками вошёл в него.

uk.L: Сказавши це, Ісус вийшов зі своїми учнями на другий бік зимового потоку Кедрон, де був сад, до якого ввійшов {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} і {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} учні.
uk.B: Сказавши це, Ісус вийшов зі своїми учнями й перейшов долину Кедрон. Там був сад, і {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} зі своїми учнями ввійшов до нього.
uk.R: Коли Ісус закінчив молитися, {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} вийшов зі своїми учнями з міста й перейшов долину Кедрон. По той бік був сад, і Ісус зі своїми учнями ввійшов туди.

ja.L: これらのことを言われると、イエスは弟子たちとともに、ケドロンの冬の谷川の向こうへ出て行かれた。そこには園があり、イエスは弟子たちとともにその中に入られた。
ja.B: これらのことを話し終えると、イエスは弟子たちとともに出て行き、ケドロンの谷を渡られた。そこには園があって、イエスは弟子たちとともにそこに入られた。
ja.R: 祈り終えると、イエスは弟子たちといっしょに町を出て、ケドロンの谷を渡られました。向こう側には園があり、イエスは弟子たちといっしょにその中に入られました。

id.L: Setelah mengatakan hal-hal itu, Yesus keluar bersama murid-murid-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}} ke seberang sungai Kidron yang mengalir di musim dingin; di sana ada sebuah taman, dan {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} masuk ke dalamnya bersama murid-murid-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}.
id.B: Sesudah Yesus mengatakan semua itu, {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} keluar bersama murid-murid-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}} dan menyeberangi Lembah Kidron. Di sana ada sebuah taman, dan {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} serta murid-murid-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}} masuk ke dalamnya.
id.R: Sesudah Yesus selesai berdoa, {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} meninggalkan kota bersama murid-murid-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}} dan menyeberangi Lembah Kidron. Di seberangnya ada sebuah taman, dan Yesus serta murid-murid-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}} masuk ke sana.

zh.L: 耶稣说了这些话，就和{{deity_pronoun:他|祂}}的门徒出去，到了汲沦冬季溪流的对岸；那里有一个园子，{{deity_pronoun:他|祂}}和{{deity_pronoun:他|祂}}的门徒进了那园子。
zh.B: 耶稣说完这些话，就和{{deity_pronoun:他|祂}}的门徒出去，过了汲沦谷。那里有一个园子，{{deity_pronoun:他|祂}}和{{deity_pronoun:他|祂}}的门徒都进去了。
zh.R: 耶稣祷告完了，就和{{deity_pronoun:他|祂}}的门徒出城，过了汲沦谷。对面有一个园子，耶稣和{{deity_pronoun:他|祂}}的门徒走了进去。

ar.L: ولمّا قال يسوع هذا الكلام، خرج مع تلاميذه إلى ما وراء سيل قدرون الشتويّ، حيث كان بستان، فدخله هو وتلاميذه.
ar.B: بعد أن قال يسوع هذا، خرج مع تلاميذه وعبر وادي قدرون. وكان هناك بستان، فدخل إليه هو وتلاميذه.
ar.R: وعندما أنهى يسوع صلاته، غادر المدينة مع تلاميذه، وعبر وادي قدرون. وكان على الجانب الآخر بستان، فدخله يسوع وتلاميذه.

fa.L: عیسی چون این سخنان را گفت، با شاگردان خود به آن سوی نهر فصلی قدرون رفت، که در آن‌جا باغی بود، و او و شاگردانش وارد آن شدند.
fa.B: عیسی پس از گفتن این سخنان، با شاگردانش بیرون رفت و از درهٔ قدرون گذشت. آن‌جا باغی بود، و او و شاگردانش وارد آن شدند.
fa.R: عیسی وقتی دعایش را به پایان رساند، با پیروانش از شهر بیرون رفت و از درهٔ قدرون گذشت. آن سوی دره باغی بود، و عیسی و پیروانش وارد آن شدند.

pa.L: ਇਹ ਗੱਲਾਂ ਆਖ ਕੇ ਯਿਸੂ ਆਪਣੇ ਚੇਲਿਆਂ ਸਮੇਤ ਕਿਦਰੋਨ ਨਾਲੇ ਦੇ ਪਾਰ ਨਿੱਕਲ ਗਏ, ਜਿੱਥੇ ਇੱਕ ਬਾਗ਼ ਸੀ, ਜਿਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਉਹ ਅਤੇ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਚੇਲੇ ਵੜੇ।
pa.B: ਜਦੋਂ ਯਿਸੂ ਇਹ ਗੱਲਾਂ ਕਹਿ ਚੁੱਕੇ, ਤਾਂ ਉਹ ਆਪਣੇ ਚੇਲਿਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਨਾਲ ਲੈ ਕੇ ਬਾਹਰ ਗਏ ਅਤੇ ਕਿਦਰੋਨ ਵਾਦੀ ਨੂੰ ਪਾਰ ਕੀਤਾ। ਉੱਥੇ ਇੱਕ ਬਾਗ਼ ਸੀ, ਅਤੇ ਉਹ ਆਪਣੇ ਚੇਲਿਆਂ ਸਮੇਤ ਉਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਚਲੇ ਗਏ।
pa.R: ਪ੍ਰਾਰਥਨਾ ਖ਼ਤਮ ਕਰਕੇ ਯਿਸੂ ਆਪਣੇ ਚੇਲਿਆਂ ਨਾਲ ਸ਼ਹਿਰ ਤੋਂ ਬਾਹਰ ਗਏ ਅਤੇ ਕਿਦਰੋਨ ਵਾਦੀ ਲੰਘ ਗਏ। ਦੂਜੇ ਪਾਸੇ ਇੱਕ ਬਾਗ਼ ਸੀ। ਯਿਸੂ ਅਤੇ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਚੇਲੇ ਉਸ ਬਾਗ਼ ਵਿੱਚ ਗਏ।

decisions.choice: having said these things: after the prayer of chapter 17, Jesus leaves for the place of his arrest
alternatives: after the farewell words of chapters 13-17 as a whole
decisions.reason: "These things" points back to what Jesus has just said, the prayer of chapter 17, which closes the words he spoke to his disciples at the supper (13:31-17:26). In 14:31 he had said, "Rise, let us go from here"; only now does John tell of their going out, from the house where they ate and out of the city.

decisions.choice: the winter stream of the Kidron: the valley east of Jerusalem, whose stream flows only in the rainy season
alternatives: a river that flows all year
decisions.reason: The word χειμάρρου means a stream that runs in winter, when the rains come, and is dry for the rest of the year; it is used of the valley it runs through. The Kidron Valley lies between the eastern wall of Jerusalem and the Mount of Olives. At Passover, in spring, it may have held little water. King David crossed the Kidron when he fled from Jerusalem, betrayed by his counselor (2 Samuel 15:23, 31); John does not draw attention to that.

decisions.choice: a garden: an enclosed plot, probably of olive trees, on the slope of the Mount of Olives
decisions.reason: John says only "a garden". Matthew and Mark name the place Gethsemane (Matthew 26:36; Mark 14:32), a name meaning "oil press", and Luke places it on the Mount of Olives (Luke 22:39). John will also place Jesus's tomb in a garden (19:41).

decisions.choice: of the Kidron, the name of the valley (SBLGNT)
alternatives: of the cedars (many manuscripts, among them some of the oldest)
decisions.reason: The name Kidron sounds like the Greek word for cedar, and many manuscripts, some of them early, read "the winter stream of the cedars". The SBLGNT reads the place name, which is certainly what is meant: the valley is called the Kidron in the Old Testament (2 Samuel 15:23; 1 Kings 15:13). A footnote gives the other reading. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the winter stream of the Kidron (L); the Kidron Valley (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word for a seasonal stream (meaning decision m2). Balanced and Readable name the valley, which is what a reader can picture and find on a map, since the stream was dry for much of the year.

decisions.choice: had finished praying; left the city; On the other side
alternatives: having said these things; went out (Literal)
decisions.reason: Readable says what "these things" were (the prayer just ended, meaning decision m1) and where Jesus went out from. "On the other side" gives the sense of "across" in a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: el torrente Cedrón (L, B); el valle del Cedrón (R); huerto
decisions.reason: Spanish "torrente" is a stream that runs only after rain, the sense of meaning decision m2, so Literal and Balanced can keep it; Readable names the valley, which the reader can picture, as the English does. "Huerto" is a planted plot of trees or crops (meaning decision m3); "jardín" suggests an ornamental garden.

decisions.choice: terminó de orar; salió de la ciudad; Al otro lado
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says what "these things" were and where Jesus went out from (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B), with Literal keeping John's present tense ("il vient", "il dit", verses 3-5); passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level
alternatives: passé composé for narration at every level
decisions.reason: The French brief for the passage (18:1-14), as in 1:19. Literal keeps the historic present where John uses it, as the English Literal does; Balanced narrates in the passé simple ("sortit", "arrêtèrent"), the tense of written narrative; Readable uses the passé composé ("a quitté", "ont arrêté"). Inside speech every level uses the passé composé ("je vous ai dit").

decisions.choice: le torrent du Cédron (L); la vallée du Cédron (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Torrent" is the French word for a stream that runs only after rain, the sense of the Greek (meaning decision m2); Balanced and Readable name the valley that Jesus crossed, as the English does.

decisions.choice: L keeps the historic present where the Greek has it ("anakuja" 18:3, "anawaambia" 18:4, 18:5); B tells the story with -li- for the first verb and -ka- for those that follow; R uses the plain past
decisions.reason: John tells some of the arrest in the present tense to make it vivid (English rendering decision r-en-1 at 18:3). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable use the narrative past, which is how written Swahili tells a story. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: kijito cha masika cha Kidroni (L); bonde la Kidroni (B, R)
alternatives: kijito cha Kidroni at every level
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a stream that runs only in the rainy season (meaning decision m2); "kijito cha masika" (a stream of the rains) says exactly that at Literal. Balanced and Readable name the valley, as the English does.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on free pronouns and possessives ("yeye", "naye", "wake", "mimi")
alternatives: a span wherever the English has one
decisions.reason: Swahili marks most pronouns inside the verb ("akimsaliti", "walimfunga"), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so the Swahili has fewer spans than the English. A pronoun at the start of a sentence ("Mimi ndiye") is written plainly with its capital. This applies to the whole passage.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change; respect is carried by the honorific -si-, 께서 and 그분 at every level (style guide section 7).

decisions.choice: 기드론 겨울 시내 (L); 기드론 골짜기 (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek "winter stream", a brook that runs only in the rainy season; Balanced and Readable name the valley, as the English does.

decisions.choice: a torrente do Cedrom (L); o vale do Cedrom (B, R)

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in the Amharic
alternatives: Marking pronouns for God and Jesus in some other way
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting that capitalises pronouns for God and Jesus in English has nothing to change in Amharic; most such pronouns are verb suffixes in any case.

decisions.choice: "የቄድሮን የክረምት ወንዝ" (the Kidron's rainy-season stream, L), "የቄድሮን ሸለቆ" (the Kidron Valley, B, R); "የአትክልት ስፍራ" (garden)
decisions.reason: In Ethiopia "ክረምት" is the rainy season, so "የክረምት ወንዝ" says exactly what the Greek "winter stream" means, a stream that flows only in the rains. "ገነት" is avoided because it suggests Eden or paradise.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in this passage
decisions.reason: The English capitalises the pronouns for Jesus under the deity_pronoun setting. Devanagari has no capital letters, so the Hindi has no span; respect comes from the honorific third person (यीशु निकले, उनके चेले) at every level (style guide, sections 4 and 7).

decisions.choice: "किद्रोन के बरसाती नाले" (L); "किद्रोन घाटी" (B, R)

decisions.choice: "зимний поток Кедрон" (L); "долина Кедрон" (B, R)

decisions.choice: "зимовий потік Кедрон" (L); "долина Кедрон" (B, R)

decisions.choice: "ケドロンの冬の谷川" (L); "ケドロンの谷" (B, R); "園" for the garden
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a stream that runs only in the rainy season (m2): Literal says so, and Balanced and Readable name the valley, as the English does. 園 is an enclosed planted plot (m3); 庭 would suggest a house garden.

decisions.choice: "sungai Kidron yang mengalir di musim dingin" (L); "Lembah Kidron" (B, R)

decisions.choice: "سيل قدرون الشتويّ" (L), "وادي قدرون" (B, R)

decisions.choice: "بستان"

decisions.reason: The Kidron is a stream that runs only in the rainy season, in a valley east of Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: the one handing him over: betraying him, and doing it now
alternatives: the one who would later hand him over
decisions.reason: As in 6:64 and 6:71, the verb means to hand someone over, and for Judas it means betrayal. Here the participle is present: the betrayal is already under way. Judas left the supper to do it (13:27-30).

decisions.choice: had often gathered there: the garden was a regular meeting place
decisions.reason: The adverb means "often", and the verb is the ordinary one for coming together. Luke says Jesus went to the Mount of Olives "as was his custom" (Luke 22:39; compare 21:37). Because it was their habit, Judas knew where to find him at night, away from the crowds.

decisions.choice: handing over (L); betraying (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 6:64 and 6:71 (rendering decision r-en-1 there): Literal keeps the plain sense of the verb, so that the reader sees it is the word later used of the authorities and of Pilate (18:30, 35; 19:16); Balanced and Readable say what Judas's handing over was (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: entregaba (L); traicionaba (B, R)
decisions.reason: As at 6:71 and 13:2: Literal keeps the plain verb "entregar", the one used later of the authorities and of Pilate (18:30, 35; 19:16); Balanced and Readable say what it means for Judas (meaning decision m1). The imperfect shows the betrayal already under way.

decisions.choice: kumtoa (L); kumsaliti (B, R)
decisions.reason: As at 6:64 and 6:71: Literal keeps the plain sense "hand over", the verb later used of the authorities and of Pilate; Balanced and Readable say what Judas's handing over was, as the English does.

decisions.choice: 넘겨주다 (L); 배반하다 (B, R) for paradidōmi
decisions.reason: As earlier in the book (6:64; 13:2; 13:21): Literal keeps the Greek verb, Balanced and Readable say what Judas was doing.

decisions.choice: "አሳልፎ የሚሰጠው" (the one handing him over) at every level
decisions.reason: "አሳልፎ መስጠት" means both to hand over and to betray, as the Greek verb does, so one Amharic phrase serves where the English uses "handing over" at Literal and "betraying" at Balanced and Readable; it is the phrase Matthew 26 and 27 use, and it links Judas's act with 18:30, 18:35 and 19:16.

decisions.choice: "जो उन्हें सौंप रहा था" (L); "जो उन्हें पकड़वा रहा था" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 6:64, 12:4 and 13:21: Literal keeps the plain sense of the verb, "hand over"; Balanced and Readable say what Judas's handing over was (meaning decision m1) with Matthew's word "पकड़वाना", to have someone arrested. The same in 18:5.

decisions.choice: "предающий" (L); "предавал" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Russian "предавать" means both handing over and betraying, so every level can use the one verb; Literal keeps the participle in the present, as the Greek has it.

decisions.choice: "видавати" (L, B); "зраджувати" (R), through chapters 18-19 for Judas
decisions.reason: The passion term settled in Matthew and Mark: the Greek verb is "hand over"; for Judas "видати" keeps both the handing over and the betrayal, and Readable names the betrayal plainly. Handing Jesus over to the authorities is "передати" (verses 30, 35; 19:11, 16).

decisions.choice: "引き渡そうとしている" (L); "裏切ろうとしていた" (B, R); also 18:5
decisions.reason: The verb is "hand over", which for Judas means betrayal (m1). Literal keeps the verb and its present tense; Balanced and Readable say what the act is, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "要把他交出去" (L); "出卖" (B, R)
alternatives: "出卖" at every level, as Matthew 26:48
decisions.reason: As the English: Literal keeps the plain verb "hand over" ("交出去"), the word later used of the authorities handing Jesus to Pilate; Balanced and Readable say what Judas is doing, "出卖", Matthew's word.

decisions.choice: "يسلّمه" (L), "يخونه" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The one handing him over is betraying him, and doing it now (m1). Literal keeps "hand over", as elsewhere in John; Balanced and Readable say "betray".

decisions.choice: "تسلیم می‌کرد" (Literal); "خیانت می‌کرد" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As for Judas throughout John.

decisions.choice: "ਜਿਹੜਾ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਸੌਂਪ ਰਿਹਾ ਸੀ" (L); "ਫੜਵਾ ਰਿਹਾ ਸੀ", "ਫੜਵਾਉਣ ਵਾਲਾ" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Greek paradidous.

source.text: ὁ οὖν Ἰούδας λαβὼν τὴν σπεῖραν καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἀρχιερέων καὶ ἐκ τῶν Φαρισαίων ὑπηρέτας ἔρχεται ἐκεῖ μετὰ φανῶν καὶ λαμπάδων καὶ ὅπλων.

records.literal_gloss: So the Judas, having taken the cohort and from the chief priests and from the Pharisees officers, comes there with lanterns and torches and weapons.

en.L: So Judas, having taken the cohort and officers from the chief priests and from the Pharisees, comes there with lanterns and torches and weapons.
en.B: So Judas went there, bringing the detachment of soldiers and temple police sent by the chief priests and the Pharisees. They carried lanterns, torches and weapons.
en.R: So Judas led a group of Roman soldiers to the garden. Temple guards sent by the leading priests and the Pharisees came with them. They brought lanterns, torches and weapons.

es.L: Judas, pues, habiendo tomado la cohorte y alguaciles de los principales sacerdotes y de los fariseos, viene allí con linternas y antorchas y armas.
es.B: Así que Judas fue allí con el destacamento de soldados y con los guardias del templo enviados por los jefes de los sacerdotes y los fariseos. Llevaban linternas, antorchas y armas.
es.R: Entonces Judas llevó al huerto a un grupo de soldados romanos. Con ellos iban unos guardias del templo, enviados por los jefes de los sacerdotes y los fariseos. Traían linternas, antorchas y armas.

fr.L: Judas donc, ayant pris la cohorte et des gardes de la part des chefs des prêtres et des Pharisiens, vient là avec des lanternes et des torches et des armes.
fr.B: Judas se rendit donc là, emmenant le détachement de soldats et des gardes du temple envoyés par les chefs des prêtres et les Pharisiens. Ils avaient des lanternes, des torches et des armes.
fr.R: Judas a donc conduit au jardin un groupe de soldats romains. Des gardes du temple, envoyés par les chefs des prêtres et les Pharisiens, venaient avec eux. Ils avaient apporté des lanternes, des torches et des armes.

sw.L: Basi Yuda, akiwa amechukua kikosi na walinzi kutoka kwa wakuu wa makuhani na kutoka kwa Mafarisayo, anakuja huko akiwa na taa, mienge na silaha.
sw.B: Basi Yuda alifika huko akiwaleta kikosi cha askari na walinzi wa hekalu waliotumwa na wakuu wa makuhani na Mafarisayo. Walikuwa na taa, mienge na silaha.
sw.R: Basi Yuda aliongoza kundi la askari wa Kirumi mpaka bustanini. Walinzi wa hekalu waliotumwa na viongozi wa makuhani na Mafarisayo walikuja pamoja nao. Walileta taa, mienge na silaha.

vi.L: Vậy Giu-đa, đem theo đội quân và các cảnh vệ từ các thầy tế lễ cả và từ những người Pha-ri-si, đến đó với đèn lồng, đuốc và vũ khí.
vi.B: Vậy Giu-đa dẫn một toán lính cùng lính canh đền thờ do các thầy tế lễ cả và người Pha-ri-si sai đến, kéo tới đó. Họ mang theo đèn lồng, đuốc và vũ khí.
vi.R: Vậy Giu-đa dẫn một toán lính La Mã đến khu vườn. Đi cùng họ có lính canh đền thờ do các thầy tế lễ đứng đầu và người Pha-ri-si sai đến. Họ mang theo đèn lồng, đuốc và vũ khí.

ko.L: 그래서 유다가 부대와, 대제사장들과 바리새파 사람들에게서 [온] 경비병들을 데리고, 등불과 횃불과 무기를 가지고 그곳으로 온다.
ko.B: 그래서 유다는 로마 군인 한 부대와, 대제사장들과 바리새파 사람들이 보낸 성전 경비병들을 데리고 그곳으로 갔다. 그들은 등불과 횃불과 무기를 들고 있었다.
ko.R: 그래서 유다는 로마 군인들을 이끌고 동산으로 왔다. 대제사장들과 바리새파 사람들이 보낸 성전 경비병들도 함께 왔다. 그들은 등불과 횃불과 무기를 들고 있었다.

pt.L: Judas, então, tendo tomado a coorte e guardas da parte dos chefes dos sacerdotes e dos fariseus, vem para lá com lanternas e tochas e armas.
pt.B: Assim Judas foi até lá, levando o destacamento de soldados e a guarda do templo enviada pelos chefes dos sacerdotes e pelos fariseus. Eles traziam lanternas, tochas e armas.
pt.R: Então Judas levou um grupo de soldados romanos até o jardim. Guardas do templo, mandados pelos chefes dos sacerdotes e pelos fariseus, foram com eles. Levavam lanternas, tochas e armas.

am.L: ስለዚህ ይሁዳ ጭፍራውንና ከካህናት አለቆችና ከፈሪሳውያን ዘበኞችን ይዞ በፋኖሶችና በችቦዎች በጦር መሣሪያዎችም ወደዚያ ይመጣል።
am.B: ስለዚህ ይሁዳ የወታደሮችን ጭፍራ፣ የካህናት አለቆችና ፈሪሳውያን የላኳቸውንም የቤተ መቅደስ ዘበኞች ይዞ ወደዚያ መጣ። ፋኖሶችን፣ ችቦዎችንና የጦር መሣሪያዎችን ይዘው ነበር።
am.R: ስለዚህ ይሁዳ የሮማውያንን ወታደሮች ቡድን እየመራ ወደ አትክልት ስፍራው መጣ። የካህናት አለቆችና ፈሪሳውያን የላኳቸው የቤተ መቅደስ ጠባቂዎችም ከእነርሱ ጋር መጡ። ፋኖሶችን፣ ችቦዎችንና የጦር መሣሪያዎችን ይዘው ነበር።

hi.L: तब यहूदा टुकड़ी को, और प्रधान याजकों और फ़रीसियों की ओर से पहरेदारों को लेकर, लालटेनों और मशालों और हथियारों के साथ वहाँ आता है।
hi.B: तब यहूदा सैनिकों की एक टुकड़ी और प्रधान याजकों और फ़रीसियों के भेजे हुए मन्दिर के पहरेदारों को साथ लेकर वहाँ गया। उनके पास लालटेनें, मशालें और हथियार थे।
hi.R: तब यहूदा रोमी सैनिकों के एक दल को बग़ीचे में ले आया। प्रधान याजकों और फ़रीसियों के भेजे हुए मन्दिर के पहरेदार भी उनके साथ आए। वे लालटेनें, मशालें और हथियार लेकर आए थे।

ru.L: Итак Иуда, взяв когорту и служителей от старших священников и от фарисеев, приходит туда с фонарями, и факелами, и оружием.
ru.B: И Иуда пришёл туда, приведя отряд солдат и храмовую стражу, присланную старшими священниками и фарисеями. У них были фонари, факелы и оружие.
ru.R: Иуда привёл в сад отряд римских солдат. С ними пришли храмовые стражники, которых прислали старшие священники и фарисеи. У них были фонари, факелы и оружие.

uk.L: Тож Юда, узявши когорту і прислужників від старших священників і від фарисеїв, приходить туди з ліхтарями, і смолоскипами, і зброєю.
uk.B: Тож Юда прийшов туди, привівши загін воїнів і храмових вартових, яких послали старші священники та фарисеї. Вони мали ліхтарі, смолоскипи та зброю.
uk.R: Тож Юда привів до саду загін римських воїнів. З ними прийшли храмові вартові, яких послали старші священники та фарисеї. Вони несли ліхтарі, смолоскипи і зброю.

ja.L: それでユダは、部隊と、祭司長たちとファリサイ派の人々からの下役たちを連れて、ともしびとたいまつと武器を持って、そこに来る。
ja.B: そこでユダは、ローマ兵の一隊と、祭司長たちやファリサイ派の人々が差し向けた神殿の警備兵たちを連れて、そこへ来た。彼らはともしびやたいまつや武器を手にしていた。
ja.R: そこでユダは、ローマの兵士たちを園に連れて来ました。祭司長たちとファリサイ派の人々が送った神殿の警備兵たちも、いっしょに来ました。彼らは、明かりやたいまつや武器を持っていました。

id.L: Lalu Yudas, dengan membawa sepasukan prajurit dan penjaga-penjaga dari imam-imam kepala dan dari orang-orang Farisi, datang ke sana dengan lentera, obor dan senjata.
id.B: Jadi Yudas pergi ke sana dengan membawa sepasukan prajurit dan penjaga-penjaga Bait Allah yang diutus oleh imam-imam kepala dan orang-orang Farisi. Mereka membawa lentera, obor dan senjata.
id.R: Jadi Yudas memimpin sekelompok prajurit Romawi ke taman itu. Penjaga-penjaga Bait Allah yang diutus oleh imam-imam kepala dan orang-orang Farisi ikut bersama mereka. Mereka membawa lentera, obor dan senjata.

zh.L: 于是犹大领了营队，以及从祭司长和从法利赛人[来]的卫兵，带着灯笼、火把和兵器，来到那里。
zh.B: 于是犹大带着一队士兵，还有祭司长和法利赛人派来的圣殿警卫，到了那里。他们拿着灯笼、火把和兵器。
zh.R: 于是犹大带着一队罗马士兵来到园子。祭司长和法利赛人派来的圣殿卫兵也跟他们一起来。他们带着灯笼、火把和武器。

ar.L: فأخذ يهوذا الكتيبة والخدّام من رؤساء الكهنة ومن الفرّيسيّين، ويأتي إلى هناك بفوانيس ومشاعل وأسلحة.
ar.B: فذهب يهوذا إلى هناك، ومعه فرقة من الجنود وحرّاس الهيكل الذين أرسلهم رؤساء الكهنة والفرّيسيّون. وكانوا يحملون فوانيس ومشاعل وأسلحة.
ar.R: فقاد يهوذا مجموعة من الجنود الرومان إلى البستان. وجاء معهم حرّاس الهيكل الذين أرسلهم كبار الكهنة والفرّيسيّون. وكانوا يحملون فوانيس ومشاعل وأسلحة.

fa.L: پس یهودا دسته‌ای از سربازان و مأمورانی از جانب سران کاهنان و فریسیان برگرفته، با فانوس‌ها و مشعل‌ها و سلاح‌ها به آن‌جا می‌آید.
fa.B: پس یهودا دسته‌ای از سربازان و نگهبانان معبد را که سران کاهنان و فریسیان فرستاده بودند، با خود به آن‌جا برد. آنان فانوس‌ها و مشعل‌ها و سلاح‌ها با خود داشتند.
fa.R: پس یهودا گروهی از سربازان رومی را به باغ آورد. نگهبانان معبد هم که سران کاهنان و فریسیان فرستاده بودند، با ایشان آمدند. فانوس و مشعل و سلاح با خود آورده بودند.

pa.L: ਸੋ ਯਹੂਦਾ ਪਲਟਨ ਨੂੰ, ਅਤੇ ਮੁੱਖ ਜਾਜਕਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਫ਼ਰੀਸੀਆਂ ਵੱਲੋਂ ਸਿਪਾਹੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਲੈ ਕੇ, ਲਾਲਟੈਣਾਂ, ਮਸ਼ਾਲਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਹਥਿਆਰਾਂ ਸਮੇਤ ਉੱਥੇ ਆਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
pa.B: ਸੋ ਯਹੂਦਾ ਸਿਪਾਹੀਆਂ ਦੀ ਇੱਕ ਟੁਕੜੀ ਅਤੇ ਮੁੱਖ ਜਾਜਕਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਫ਼ਰੀਸੀਆਂ ਦੇ ਭੇਜੇ ਹੋਏ ਹੈਕਲ ਦੇ ਪਹਿਰੇਦਾਰਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਲੈ ਕੇ ਉੱਥੇ ਪਹੁੰਚਿਆ। ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਹੱਥਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਲਾਲਟੈਣਾਂ, ਮਸ਼ਾਲਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਹਥਿਆਰ ਸਨ।
pa.R: ਸੋ ਯਹੂਦਾ ਰੋਮੀ ਸਿਪਾਹੀਆਂ ਦੇ ਇੱਕ ਦਲ ਨੂੰ ਬਾਗ਼ ਵਿੱਚ ਲੈ ਆਇਆ। ਵੱਡੇ ਜਾਜਕਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਫ਼ਰੀਸੀਆਂ ਦੇ ਘੱਲੇ ਹੋਏ ਹੈਕਲ ਦੇ ਪਹਿਰੇਦਾਰ ਵੀ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਆਏ। ਉਹ ਲਾਲਟੈਣਾਂ, ਮਸ਼ਾਲਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਹਥਿਆਰ ਚੁੱਕੀ ਆਏ ਸਨ।

decisions.choice: the cohort: a unit of Roman soldiers from the garrison in Jerusalem; John need not mean the whole unit
alternatives: the temple guard, called by a military word
the whole cohort, several hundred men
decisions.reason: The word σπεῖραν is the usual term for a Roman cohort, at full strength up to about 600 men, and in 18:12 its commander is called by the title of a Roman tribune. Acts uses the same two words for the Roman garrison in Jerusalem, which was on watch at the festivals, when crowds filled the city (Acts 21:31-32). The article may simply name the unit the soldiers came from; a detachment, not all of it, is the likely meaning. John does not say how the Roman soldiers came to be sent; their presence shows that the Roman authorities were involved from the arrest on. The other Gospels speak of a crowd sent by the chief priests (Mark 14:43).

decisions.choice: officers from the chief priests and the Pharisees: the temple police, sent by the council
decisions.reason: These are the officers who kept order in the temple for the chief priests, sent once before to arrest Jesus and come back without him (7:32, 45-46). The chief priests and the Pharisees are the leaders who met in council and gave orders for his arrest (11:47, 57).

decisions.choice: having taken: Judas brought them and guided them to the place
alternatives: Judas was in command of them
decisions.reason: Judas did not command Roman soldiers or the temple police. He took them along as the one who knew the place (verse 2); Acts 1:16 calls him "guide to those who arrested Jesus".

decisions.choice: lanterns, torches and weapons: equipment for a search at night, and for resistance
decisions.reason: A lantern held a small oil lamp shielded from the wind; a torch was a burning brand. Passover fell at the full moon, but they came prepared to search a dark garden among trees, and armed in case Jesus's followers fought.

decisions.choice: comes (L); went, led (B, R); also says (L), asked and said (B, R) in verses 4 and 5
decisions.reason: John often tells past events in the present tense ("he comes", "he says") to make a scene vivid. Literal keeps the present; Balanced and Readable use the past, as stories are normally told. This applies to every such verb in the passage ("comes" in verse 3, "says" in verses 4 and 5).

decisions.choice: the detachment of soldiers, temple police (B); a group of Roman soldiers, temple guards, leading priests (R)
decisions.reason: "Cohort" names a Roman unit that few readers know, so Balanced says "detachment of soldiers" and Readable says plainly whose soldiers they were (meaning decision m1). The officers are named as at 7:32 and 7:45: "temple police" at Balanced, "temple guards" at Readable (meaning decision m2). Readable says "leading priests", as in John 7 and 11, and splits the long sentence.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal (viene, dice); pretérito at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in John: Literal keeps John's present, which makes the scene vivid; Balanced and Readable use the pretérito, as Spanish stories are told. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: la cohorte, alguaciles, los principales sacerdotes (L); el destacamento de soldados, los guardias del templo, los jefes de los sacerdotes (B); un grupo de soldados romanos, unos guardias del templo (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Roman military term and the words John 7:32 uses at Literal for the officers and the chief priests. Balanced and Readable say who these men were (meaning decisions m1 and m2), with the terms used for them in John 7 and 11.

decisions.choice: la cohorte (L), le détachement de soldats (B), des soldats romains (R); des gardes (L), des gardes du temple (B, R); les chefs des prêtres (every level)
decisions.reason: As the English (meaning decisions m1 and m2): "cohorte" names the Roman unit at Literal, and Balanced and Readable say what it was. The officers are "gardes", the word used for them through John; "chefs des prêtres" is the book-wide French for the chief priests, kept distinct from "le grand prêtre" (verse 10).

decisions.choice: kikosi (L), kikosi cha askari (B), kundi la askari wa Kirumi (R); walinzi (L), walinzi wa hekalu (B, R); wakuu wa makuhani (L, B), viongozi wa makuhani (R)
alternatives: watumishi for the officers at Literal, as at 7:32
decisions.reason: "Kikosi" is a military unit, the sense of the Roman cohort (meaning decision m1); Readable says whose soldiers they were, as the English does. The officers are the temple police (meaning decision m2): "walinzi" at Literal and "walinzi wa hekalu" at Balanced and Readable, as at 7:32 and 7:45 (Balanced). The chief priests are "wakuu wa makuhani" at Literal and Balanced and "viongozi wa makuhani" at Readable, as in John 7-12.

decisions.choice: đội quân, cảnh vệ (L); toán lính, lính canh đền thờ (B); toán lính La Mã, lính canh đền thờ (R)
decisions.reason: The terms used elsewhere in the Vietnamese John (7:32, 7:45) for the temple police; "đội quân" at Literal names the Roman unit, "toán lính" says a detachment of it. Literal keeps the historic present "đến" (comes) by leaving out "đã", as through this passage.

decisions.choice: Historic present kept at Literal (온다, 말씀하신다); past at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: John tells these steps in the present; Literal keeps it, Balanced and Readable use the narrative past (one decision for the passage).

decisions.choice: 부대, 경비병들 (L); 로마 군인 한 부대, 성전 경비병들 (B); 로마 군인들, 성전 경비병들 (R)
decisions.reason: 부대 is a unit of soldiers without naming its size; the officers were the temple police, and 경비병 says that in modern Korean, where the older 하속 is no longer understood.

decisions.choice: guardas (L); a guarda do templo (B); guardas do templo (R)
decisions.reason: The English Literal says "officers", but Portuguese "oficiais" means military officers of rank. These were the men who kept order in the temple (meaning decision m2), so Literal says "guardas", and Balanced and Readable name the temple guard.

decisions.choice: "ጭፍራ" for the cohort (L, B), "የሮማውያን ወታደሮች ቡድን" (R); "ዘበኞች" for the officers (L), "የቤተ መቅደስ ዘበኞች" (B), "የቤተ መቅደስ ጠባቂዎች" (R)
decisions.reason: "ጭፍራ" is a body of soldiers under one command, the word Matthew 27:27 uses for the same Greek word. "ዘበኞች" (guards) is Matthew 26:58's word for the same officers; Balanced and Readable say whose guards they were, as the English does. The same words hold through 18:12, 18:18, 18:22 and 19:6.

decisions.choice: "आता है" (L); "गया", "ले आया" (B, R); likewise "कहते हैं" (L), "पूछा", "कहा" (B, R) in verses 4-5
decisions.reason: John often tells past events in the present tense. Literal keeps the historic present, Balanced and Readable use the past, as docs/john-terms.md settles; one decision for the passage.

decisions.choice: "टुकड़ी", "पहरेदार" (L); "सैनिकों की एक टुकड़ी", "मन्दिर के पहरेदार" (B); "रोमी सैनिकों का एक दल", "मन्दिर के पहरेदार" (R)
decisions.reason: The cohort is "टुकड़ी", as in Matthew 27:27 and Mark 15:16 in Hindi; Readable says whose soldiers they were (meaning decision m1). The officers are the temple police (m2): Literal says "पहरेदार", as in Mark 14:54, and Balanced and Readable add whose guards they were.

decisions.choice: "приходит" (L); "пришёл", "привёл" (B, R)
decisions.reason: John often tells past events in the present (historic present). Literal keeps it (here and in "говорит", verses 4-5); Balanced and Readable use the past, as Russian narrative does. One note for the passage.

decisions.choice: "когорта", "служители" (L); "отряд солдат", "храмовая стража" (B); "отряд римских солдат", "храмовые стражники" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Roman unit's name, as Matthew 27:27 does; Balanced and Readable say who the men were (meaning decisions m1, m2). "Старшие священники" for the chief priests, as the style guide sets.

decisions.choice: "когорта", "прислужники" (L); "загін", "храмові вартові" (B, R); "тисяцький" (L), "командир" (B, R) in verse 12
decisions.reason: The passion terms settled in Matthew and Mark: Literal keeps the Roman unit and the Greek word for attendants; Balanced and Readable say what they were, a detachment of soldiers and the temple police.

decisions.choice: "部隊" and "下役たち" (L); "ローマ兵の一隊" and "神殿の警備兵たち" (B); "ローマの兵士たち" and "神殿の警備兵たち" (R); also 18:12
decisions.reason: The cohort is a unit of Roman soldiers (m1) and the officers are the temple police of the chief priests (m2). Literal keeps general words close to the Greek; Balanced and Readable say who they were, as the English does.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal ("来る", "言われる"); past at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: John tells the arrest partly in the present. Literal keeps the Greek tense; Balanced and Readable narrate in the past, as Japanese narrative does. This holds through 18:1-14.

decisions.choice: "来到" without "了" (L); "到了", "来到" in the past (B, R); likewise "说" for "says" in this passage
decisions.reason: John often tells past events in the present ("he comes", "he says"). Chinese marks no tense, so Literal keeps the present simply by leaving the verb bare, without the completive "了"; Balanced and Readable tell the scene as past. Noted once for the passage.

decisions.choice: "营队", "卫兵" (L); "一队士兵", "圣殿警卫" (B); "一队罗马士兵", "圣殿卫兵" (R)
decisions.reason: "营队" is Matthew 27:27's word for the Roman cohort; Balanced and Readable say what it was (meaning decision m1). The officers are the temple police (meaning decision m2): "卫兵" at Literal as Matthew 26:58, "圣殿警卫" / "圣殿卫兵" at Balanced and Readable. "祭司长" and "法利赛人" are the glossary's words at every level; Readable keeps "祭司长" where the English Readable says "leading priests".

decisions.choice: "الكتيبة" (L), "فرقة من الجنود" (B), "مجموعة من الجنود الرومان" (R)
decisions.reason: The cohort is a unit of Roman soldiers from the garrison in Jerusalem; John need not mean the whole unit (m1). Balanced and Readable avoid a word that suggests hundreds of men.

decisions.choice: "الخدّام" (L), "حرّاس الهيكل" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The officers from the chief priests and the Pharisees are the temple police, sent by the council (m2), as in 7:32.

decisions.choice: historic present "ويأتي"
decisions.reason: The Greek tells this step with a present verb; Literal keeps it, and Balanced and Readable use the past.

decisions.choice: "می‌آید", "می‌گوید" (Literal); the past (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps John's historic present through 18:3-5.

records.literal_gloss: Jesus therefore, knowing all the things coming upon him, went out, and says to them, "Whom do you seek?"

en.L: So Jesus, knowing all the things that were coming upon {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, went out and says to them, "Whom are you seeking?"
en.B: Jesus knew everything that was about to happen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went out to them and asked, "Who is it you are looking for?"
en.R: Jesus knew everything that was going to happen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went out to meet them and asked, "Who are you looking for?"

es.L: Jesús, pues, sabiendo todas las cosas que venían sobre {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, salió, y les dice: «¿A quién {{plural_you:buscan|buscáis}}?».
es.B: Jesús sabía todo lo que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} iba a suceder, así que salió hacia ellos y les preguntó: «¿A quién {{plural_you:buscan|buscáis}}?».
es.R: Jesús sabía todo lo que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} iba a pasar. Por eso salió a su encuentro y les preguntó: «¿A quién {{plural_you:buscan|buscáis}}?».

fr.L: Jésus donc, sachant tout ce qui venait sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, sortit, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Qui cherchez-vous ? »
fr.B: Jésus savait tout ce qui allait {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} arriver ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sortit donc vers eux et leur demanda : « Qui cherchez-vous ? »
fr.R: Jésus savait tout ce qui allait {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} arriver. Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est sorti à leur rencontre et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur a demandé : « Qui cherchez-vous ? »

sw.L: Basi Yesu, akijua mambo yote yaliyokuwa yakimjia, alitoka, na anawaambia, "Mnamtafuta nani?"
sw.B: Yesu alijua yote yaliyokuwa karibu kumpata, basi akatoka kuwaendea, akawauliza, "Ni nani mnayemtafuta?"
sw.R: Yesu alijua kila kitu kilichokuwa kitampata. Basi akatoka kwenda kukutana nao, akawauliza, "Mnamtafuta nani?"

vi.R: Đức Giê-xu biết mọi việc sắp xảy ra cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Vì thế {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi ra gặp họ và hỏi: "Các người tìm ai?"

ko.L: 그래서 예수께서는 자기에게 닥쳐올 모든 일을 아시고 나가셔서 그들에게 말씀하신다. "너희는 누구를 찾느냐?"

pt.L: Jesus, então, sabendo todas as coisas que vinham sobre {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}, saiu e lhes diz: "A quem vocês procuram?"
pt.B: Jesus sabia tudo o que estava para {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} acontecer, e por isso saiu ao encontro deles e perguntou: "Quem vocês estão procurando?"
pt.R: Jesus sabia tudo o que ia acontecer com {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}. Por isso saiu para encontrar os homens e perguntou: "Quem vocês estão procurando?"

hi.L: तब यीशु, जो कुछ उन पर आनेवाला था सब जानकर, बाहर निकले और उनसे कहते हैं, "तुम किसे ढूँढ़ते हो?"

ru.L: Иисус же, зная всё, что должно было с {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}} произойти, вышел и говорит им: «Кого ищете?»

uk.L: Тож Ісус, знаючи все, що мало прийти на {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}}, вийшов і каже їм: «Кого шукаєте?»

ja.L: それでイエスは、ご自分に降りかかろうとしていることをすべて知っておられ、出て行って、彼らに言われる。「だれを捜しているのか？」
ja.B: イエスは、ご自分の身に起ころうとしていることをすべて知っておられたので、進み出て、「だれを捜しているのか？」と言われた。

decisions.choice: knowing all that was coming upon him: Jesus goes to meet his arrest knowingly and by his own choice
decisions.reason: John has said that Jesus knew his hour had come (13:1) and knew all that the Father had given into his hands (13:3). He is not caught by surprise: he steps forward himself. He had said that no one takes his life from him, but that he lays it down of his own accord (10:18).

decisions.choice: went out: came out of the garden to meet them
alternatives: stepped forward from among his disciples
decisions.reason: In verse 1 Jesus and his disciples went into the garden; now he goes out toward the men coming for him. The word may also mean only that he stepped forward. Either way he meets them before they find him.

decisions.choice: Whom are you seeking?: Jesus makes them name the one they have come for
decisions.reason: "Seek" runs through John's Gospel. Jesus's first words in it are "What are you seeking?" (1:38), and after the resurrection he asks Mary, "Whom are you seeking?" (20:15). Here those who seek him seek to arrest him, as others had sought to kill him (5:18; 7:1, 30). His question leads them to say his name (verse 5).

decisions.choice: went out to them (B); went out to meet them (R); asked (B, R); Who (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whom he went out toward (meaning decision m2) and use "asked" for the present "says" before a question (historic present, rendering decision r-en-1 at verse 3). Literal keeps the formal "whom"; Balanced and Readable use everyday "who".

decisions.choice: salió hacia ellos (B); salió a su encuentro (R); ¿A quién buscan? (every level)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whom he went out toward (meaning decision m2). Every level keeps "buscar", the verb of Jesus's questions in 1:38 and 20:15 (meaning decision m3); Spanish needs no fuller form to sound natural.

decisions.choice: Qui cherchez-vous ?
decisions.reason: French "chercher" covers both "seek" and "look for", so every level asks the same short question, which keeps the echo of 1:38 and 20:15 and the repetition of verse 7.

decisions.choice: Jesus says "Ta" for himself and "các người" to the arresting party
decisions.reason: The style guide's forms of address: Jesus speaks to opponents and officials as "các người", which keeps distance without contempt.

decisions.choice: "{{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}}"
decisions.reason: Russian needs the form "ним" after a preposition; it takes the setting like "него" and "нему" in the style guide's list.

decisions.choice: Jesus speaks to the arresting party in the plain style with authority ("だれを捜しているのか"); the soldiers answer plainly ("ナザレのイエスだ")
alternatives: polite "だれを捜しているのですか"
decisions.reason: Jesus takes the lead in the scene (m1, m3); the plain question sounds like one in command, not a petitioner. The arresting men owe no courtesy to the man they have come to seize, so their answer is plain.

decisions.choice: "إذ كان عالمًا" (L), "وكان ... يعرف ... فخرج" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Jesus goes to meet his arrest knowingly and by his own choice (m1); the knowing is set before the going out.

decisions.choice: the Nazorean: the man from Nazareth
alternatives: a title with a further meaning, such as a play on the "branch" of Isaiah 11:1
decisions.reason: The word Ναζωραῖος is one of two forms used in the New Testament of Jesus as the man from Nazareth; Mark uses the other (Mark 1:24; 14:67), and both mean the same thing (compare Acts 2:22; 22:8). John uses this form only in the arrest and on the notice over the cross (18:5, 7; 19:19). Nazareth was a small town in Galilee, and Jesus was known by it (1:45-46). Matthew links the name with the words of the prophets (Matthew 2:23); John makes no such link. A footnote gives the form of the word.

decisions.choice: the Nazorean (L); of Nazareth (B); from Nazareth (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the form of the word as a title; Balanced and Readable say what it means (meaning decision m1). Balanced and Readable leave out "him" after "answered", which English does not need.

decisions.choice: el Nazoreo (L); de Nazaret (B); el de Nazaret (R); A Jesús
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the form of the word as a title, as the English does; Balanced and Readable say what it means (meaning decision m1). "A Jesús" answers "¿A quién ...?" and mirrors the Greek object case.

decisions.choice: Jésus le Nazôréen (L); de Nazareth (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the form John uses (meaning decision m1) in the usual French spelling of scholarly translations, "Nazôréen"; Balanced and Readable say where he was from, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Mnazareti (L); wa Nazareti (B); kutoka Nazareti (R)
alternatives: a coined form copying the Greek spelling
decisions.reason: "Mnazareti" is the ordinary Swahili word for a man of Nazareth and keeps the word as a title at Literal; a form copying the Greek spelling would be unknown to readers. Balanced and Readable say where he came from, as the English does. The same in verse 7.

decisions.choice: "Giê-xu" without the honorific "Đức" in the mouths of the arresting party; Na-xa-rét
decisions.reason: The soldiers and officers do not honour Jesus, so they name him plainly, as the man born blind does before he believes (9:11). "Na-xa-rét" is the established Protestant spelling of Nazareth.

decisions.choice: The arresting party answers Jesus in the plain style (해라체)
decisions.reason: They have come to arrest him and do not treat him as a superior; the guide allows opponents to speak to Jesus without honorifics where the scene is hostile.

decisions.choice: 나사렛 사람 (L); 나사렛 (B); 나사렛에서 온 (R) for "the Nazorean"
decisions.reason: The title means the man from Nazareth; Literal keeps it as a title with 사람.

decisions.choice: o nazareno
decisions.reason: Portuguese has one current word for a man from Nazareth, "nazareno", used for this same Greek form in Matthew 26:71; "nazoreu" is a scholar's transliteration few readers know. Balanced and Readable say "de Nazaré", as the English does.

decisions.choice: "ናዝራዊው" (the Nazorean, L); "የናዝሬቱ" (of Nazareth, B); "ከናዝሬት የመጣው" (from Nazareth, R); also 18:7
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek's descriptive title, as the English Literal does; Balanced uses the phrase of Matthew 26:71, and Readable says it plainly.

decisions.choice: "नासरी" (L); "नासरत के" (B); "नासरत वाले" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the form of the word as a title, Balanced and Readable say what it means, the man from Nazareth (meaning decision m1), as in Mark 14:67 in Hindi.

decisions.choice: "Иисуса Назорея" (L); "Иисуса из Назарета" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word here is Nazoraios, so Literal says "Назорей", as settled in Luke; Balanced and Readable say what it means (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "Назорей" (L, B); "з Назарета" (R), also in verse 7 and 19:19
decisions.reason: The Greek word is the one Matthew uses ("Назорей"), kept apart from Mark's other form ("Назарянин"); Readable says plainly where he came from.

decisions.choice: "ナザレ人イエス" (L); "ナザレのイエス" (B); "ナザレから来たイエス" (R); also 18:7 and 19:19
decisions.reason: The word means the man from Nazareth (m1). Literal says "ナザレ人", a man of Nazareth, keeping the Greek's noun of origin; Balanced and Readable say where he came from. The same forms are used in Acts.

decisions.choice: "拿撒勒人耶稣" (L); "拿撒勒的耶稣" (B); "从拿撒勒来的耶稣" (R)
decisions.reason: Matthew 26:71's wording for the same Greek title, level by level: Literal keeps it as a title, Balanced and Readable say it names his town (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "الناصريّ" (L, B), "الذي من الناصرة" (R)
decisions.reason: The Nazorean is the man from Nazareth (m1). "الناصريّ" is the familiar Arabic form; Readable says where he is from.

decisions.choice: "عیسای ناصری" (Literal); "عیسای اهل ناصره" (Balanced); "عیسی از ناصره" (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the title form; the others say where he was from.

decisions.choice: "ਨਾਸਰੀ" (L); "ਨਾਸਰਤ ਦੇ" (B); "ਨਾਸਰਤ ਵਾਲੇ" (R)
decisions.reason: Greek Nazoraios.

pa.L: ਉਹ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਕਹਿੰਦੇ ਹਨ, "ਮੈਂ [ਉਹੀ] ਹਾਂ।"

pa.R: ਯਿਸੂ ਨੇ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਦੱਸਿਆ, "ਮੈਂ ਉਹੀ ਹਾਂ।"

decisions.choice: I am: first of all "I am he", the man you are looking for; the words also echo the way God names himself, which verse 6 brings out
alternatives: the bare "I am", the divine name, as the main sense
only the plain sense, with no echo
decisions.reason: The words have no predicate, but the question supplies one: they are seeking Jesus of Nazareth, and he says he is that man. Verse 8 takes the words up in that sense: "I told you that I am he; so if you are seeking me, let these men go." Yet John repeats the words three times (verses 5, 6 and 8), and when Jesus says them, the men who came to arrest him draw back and fall to the ground (verse 6). "I am" is how God speaks of himself in the Greek of Isaiah (Isaiah 43:10; compare Exodus 3:14), and Jesus has used the words of himself with nothing after them (8:24, 28, 58; 13:19). Here, unlike 8:58, a plain sense fits the words, so it is taken as uppermost, and the echo of God's name is heard within it, as at 6:20. Marked uncertain because the weight between the two senses is a judgment. A footnote gives the bare "I am".

decisions.choice: I am [he] (L); I am he (B, R); also verses 6 and 8
decisions.reason: Because the plain sense is uppermost here (meaning decision m1), every level supplies "he", in brackets at Literal as at 6:20, and it takes the deity_pronoun setting as a pronoun for Christ. "I am he" is also the English used for God's words in Isaiah 43:10 and Deuteronomy 32:39, so the echo can still be heard, which "It is I" or "I am the one" would lose. The same words stand at verses 5, 6 and 8 so the reader sees the repetition. "Said" and "told" stand for the present "says" (rendering decision r-en-1 at verse 3). The footnote gives the bare "I am".

decisions.choice: Yo soy, at every level; also verses 6 and 8
decisions.reason: In Spanish "Yo soy" is a complete answer to a question about who someone is ("I am the one"), so it gives the plain sense that meaning decision m1 finds uppermost and still keeps the words John uses for the echo of God's name (8:24, 8:28, 13:19). English needs "he" for the plain sense; Spanish does not. "Soy yo" (as at 6:20) would lose the echo that John draws out by repeating the words, and "Yo soy él" is not natural Spanish.

decisions.choice: Jesús
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker, since the soldiers have just been the subject.

decisions.choice: Je [le] suis (L); Je le suis (B); C’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} (R); the same in verses 6 and 8
decisions.reason: Meaning decision m1 takes the plain sense, "I am the man you seek", as uppermost, with an echo of God's name. French "Je le suis" gives that sense while keeping the words "je ... suis" visible, so the repetition and the link with 8:24, 8:28, 8:58 and 13:19 can still be seen; Literal brackets the "le" that the Greek lacks. Here "le" stands for the predicate ("Jésus le Nazôréen"), not for a person, so unlike the English "he" it takes no deity_pronoun setting. Readable says "C’est moi", the everyday answer, where the pronoun for Jesus does take the setting. The footnote of m1 gives the bare "Je suis".

decisions.choice: "Mimi ndiye" at every level, without brackets; also verses 6 and 8
decisions.reason: The plain sense is uppermost here (meaning decision m1): Jesus is the man they are looking for. "Ndiye" is the copula with "he" built into it (I am he, I am the one), so Swahili needs no bracketed word where the English Literal has "[he]", and there is no free pronoun after it for the reader setting. "Mimi niko", used where the words stand alone (8:24; 13:19), would lose the answer to their question; the echo of God's name is left to the meaning notes.

decisions.choice: Ta là [người đó] (L); Chính Ta đây (B); Ta đây (R)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese cannot leave "I am" without a complement, so the bare words that echo God's name cannot be kept; the meaning decision's footnote gives that echo. "Ta đây" (here I am) is how a person answers to his name, and "chính" stresses that he is the very one. Also verses 6 and 8.

decisions.choice: 내가 [그 사람]이다 (L); 내가 그 사람이다 (B); 내가 바로 그 사람이다 (R) for egō eimi, also in verses 6 and 8
decisions.reason: Korean must say who "I am" is, so the plain sense the English follows is given; the echo of God's name cannot be kept in Korean wording and is left to the meaning note and its footnote.

decisions.choice: Eu sou, with nothing supplied (also verse 6)
decisions.reason: Portuguese answers a question about who someone is with "Eu sou" alone ("I am the one"), so the plain sense that the English supplies "he" for (meaning decision m1) needs no added word, and the echo of God's name stays audible. "Eu sou ele" is not Portuguese; "Sou eu" ("It's me") would lose the echo.

decisions.choice: "እኔ ነኝ" (I am, it is I) at every level; also 18:6 and 18:8
alternatives: "የምትፈልጉት እኔ ነኝ" (I am the one you want)
decisions.reason: Amharic "እኔ ነኝ" is both the plain answer "I am he" and, word for word, "I am", so it keeps both senses the meaning decision describes without brackets or a choice between them.

decisions.choice: "मैं [वही] हूँ" (L); "मैं वही हूँ" (B, R); also verses 6 and 8
decisions.reason: The plain sense, "I am the man you are looking for", is uppermost here (meaning decision m1), so every level supplies "वही", in brackets at Literal, as the English supplies "he". The bare "मैं हूँ" is kept for the absolute sayings (8:58), and the Literal bracket shows that the Greek has only "I am".

decisions.choice: "[यीशु] उनसे कहते हैं" (L)
decisions.reason: The honorific "वे" for Jesus would read like "they" beside the plural of the arresting party, so Literal names him in brackets (style guide, section 4).

decisions.choice: "Это {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}}" at every level, here and in verses 6 and 8
decisions.reason: As in the English, the plain sense "it is I, the man you seek" is uppermost (meaning decision m1), so Russian says "Это я", the natural answer, with the setting on the pronoun; the echo of God's name is noted in the meaning decision. The absolute "I am" elsewhere in John (8:24, 8:28, 8:58, 13:19) is "Я есть".

decisions.choice: "ответил"
decisions.reason: Readable says "answered", since Jesus is replying to the soldiers; the English Readable says "told them".

decisions.choice: "Це Я" (with "[Це]" in brackets at L), also in verses 6 and 8
decisions.reason: The settled convention for 18:5-8: the plain sense, "I am the one you seek", comes first (meaning decision m1), and Ukrainian needs "це" to say it. Literal brackets "це" so the bare Greek "I am" and its echo of God's name (8:58, "Я є") stay visible.

decisions.choice: "わたしである" at every level, in 18:5, 18:6 and 18:8
decisions.reason: The words first answer their question, "I am he" (m1), and わたしである says that plainly while its solemn form leaves room for the echo of God's name that verse 6 brings out. "わたしはある", used where no predicate can be supplied, would lose the plain sense here; "わたしだ" would lose the weight.

decisions.choice: "Aku ini" at every level, here and in verses 6 and 8
decisions.reason: m1: first of all "I am he", the man they are looking for, with an echo of God's name brought out by verse 6. The glossary gives "Aku ini" for 18:5-8 (Terms, section 1): the plain answer of someone who identifies himself, which leaves the echo to the footnote of m1. Uncertain, with "Akulah Dia" (as at 8:24) as the alternative.

decisions.choice: "我就是[{{deity_pronoun:他|祂}}]" (L); "我就是" (B, R), with no deity_pronoun span at Balanced and Readable; also verses 6 and 8
decisions.reason: Here "I am" first of all means "I am he", the Jesus of Nazareth they seek (meaning decision m1), so it takes John's form for "I am he" (as 4:26): Literal brackets the pronoun the English supplies, in its span; Balanced and Readable say "我就是", which needs no pronoun after the verb, so there is nothing to span where the English spans "He". "我是" stays at the heart of the phrase, so the echo of God's "I am" that verse 6 brings out is still heard; "是我" ("it's me") would lose it. The bare "我是" of 8:24, 28, 58 and 13:19 is kept for "I am" with no predicate at all.

decisions.choice: "أنا هو" at every level, also in verses 6 and 8
decisions.reason: "I am" means first of all "I am he", the man you are looking for, and the words also echo the way God names himself, which verse 6 brings out (m1). "أنا هو" carries both, as in 8:24, 8:28 and 13:19.

decisions.choice: "من [همان] هستم" (Literal); "من همان هستم" (Balanced, Readable); also in verses 6 and 8
decisions.reason: In the garden the words answer the question, so "همان" is supplied; "من ... هستم" still echoes John 8:58, and the soldiers falling back shows the weight of it.

decisions.choice: "[عیسی]" supplied (Literal)
decisions.reason: Names the speaker in brackets.

decisions.choice: "ਮੈਂ [ਉਹੀ] ਹਾਂ" (L); "ਮੈਂ ਉਹੀ ਹਾਂ" (B, R); also verses 6 and 8
decisions.reason: Greek ego eimi without a predicate.

decisions.reason: Historic present with the honorific plural.

ko.L: 그래서 그분이 그들에게 "내가 [그 사람]이다" 하고 말씀하시자, 그들은 뒤로 물러나 땅에 쓰러졌다.

ja.L: それで、イエスが彼らに「わたしである」と言われたとき、彼らは後ずさりして、地に倒れた。

ja.R: イエスが「わたしである」と言われると、彼らは後ろに下がって、地面に倒れてしまいました。

id.L: Ketika {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} berkata kepada mereka, "Aku ini," mereka mundur dan jatuh ke tanah.

zh.L: 于是{{deity_pronoun:他|祂}}一对他们说“我就是[{{deity_pronoun:他|祂}}]”，他们就往后退，倒在地上。

pa.L: ਸੋ ਜਦੋਂ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੇ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਕਿਹਾ, "ਮੈਂ [ਉਹੀ] ਹਾਂ," ਤਾਂ ਉਹ ਪਿਛਾਂਹ ਹਟੇ ਅਤੇ ਜ਼ਮੀਨ ਉੱਤੇ ਡਿੱਗ ਪਏ।

decisions.choice: they drew back and fell to the ground: overcome by the one who spoke, they cannot take him until he allows it
alternatives: they stumbled back in surprise or fear, with no further meaning
decisions.reason: John tells it as a direct result of Jesus's words: "when he said ... they drew back and fell". In the Scriptures people fall to the ground before an appearance of God or of his messenger (Ezekiel 1:28; Daniel 10:9; Acts 9:4). The armed men who came to seize Jesus end up on the ground before him; he is arrested only because he gives himself up (10:18; verses 4 and 8).

decisions.choice: possibly the psalms in which the enemies of the righteous are turned back and fall
decisions.reason: Psalm 27:2 says of the psalmist's enemies, "they stumbled and fell", and Psalm 35:4 prays that those who seek his life may be "turned back". John does not quote these psalms, so the echo is uncertain.

decisions.choice: I am: as in verse 5, with the echo of God's name brought out by what follows
decisions.reason: See meaning decision m1 at 18:5. John repeats Jesus's words before telling of the men's fall, which shows that the words themselves, not only the surprise of being met, threw them back.

decisions.choice: I am [he] (L), I am he (B, R); went backward (L), stepped backward (B), moved back (R)
decisions.reason: "I am he" as at verse 5 (rendering decision r-en-1 there). The Greek says they "went away to the things behind", a phrase for moving backward; each level says that in plain words. Balanced and Readable name Jesus as the speaker.

decisions.choice: Yo soy; se fueron hacia atrás (L); retrocedieron (B); se echaron hacia atrás (R)
decisions.reason: "Yo soy" as in verse 5. The Greek says they "went away to the things behind"; Literal keeps the verb of going, Balanced and Readable say it plainly. Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

decisions.choice: "أنا هو"; "سقطوا" / "وقعوا على الأرض"
decisions.reason: Overcome by the one who spoke, they cannot take him until he allows it (m1); the echo of God's name in "I am" is brought out by their falling (m3).

en.B: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked them again, "Who is it you are looking for?"

fr.B: Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur demanda de nouveau : « Qui cherchez-vous ? »

pt.R: Jesus perguntou de novo a eles: "Quem vocês estão procurando?"

ru.R: Иисус снова спросил их: «Кого вы ищете?»

uk.B: Тож {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} знову запитав їх: «Кого ви шукаєте?»

ja.B: そこでイエスは、もう一度、「だれを捜しているのか？」とお尋ねになった。

zh.B: 于是{{deity_pronoun:他|祂}}再问他们：“你们要找的是谁？”
zh.R: 耶稣又问他们：“你们在找谁？”

fa.B: پس باز از ایشان پرسید: «به دنبال چه کسی هستید؟»

decisions.choice: he asked them again: Jesus keeps the lead, and makes them name him alone
decisions.reason: The men have fallen to the ground, and it is Jesus, not they, who speaks next. By asking the same question he has them say again that it is Jesus of Nazareth they want, and so he can ask that his disciples go free (verse 8).

decisions.choice: Who is it (B); Who (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 4 (rendering decision r-en-1 there). Readable names Jesus, since the men have just been the subject.

decisions.choice: volvieron a responder
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable shows that they repeat their first answer (meaning decision m1). The name as in verse 5.

records.literal_gloss: Answered Jesus, "I told you that I am; if therefore me you seek, let these to go away";

en.L: Jesus answered, "I told you that I am [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}}]. So if you are seeking {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, let these [men] go away."
en.B: Jesus replied, "I have told you that I am {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}. So if it is {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} you are looking for, let these men go."
en.R: "I told you that I am {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}," Jesus answered. "If I am the one you want, let these men go."

es.L: Respondió Jesús: «{{plural_you:Les|Os}} dije que yo soy; si, pues, a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:buscan|buscáis}}, {{plural_you:dejen|dejad}} ir a estos».
